issue_context.title: QueryBuilder not inferring entity type from `.update(YourEntity)`
issue_context.body:
### Issue description

The QueryBuilder returns a `UpdateQueryBuilder<any>` instead of correctly inferring the entity type

### Expected Behavior

Calling `.update(entity: Entity)` should return a correctly typed `UpdateQueryBuilder<Entity>`

```ts
const updateQueryBuilder = entityManager
    .createQueryBuilder()
    .update(Person);
   
// => expect updateQueryBuilder to be a UpdateQueryBuilder<Person>
```


### Actual Behavior

Calling `.update(Person)` returns a `UpdateQueryBuilder<any>`. 
However, `.update(Person, {})` returns a correctly typed `UpdateQueryBuilder<Person>`.

This suggests that a specific overload of the `update` function is not correctly typed:
```ts
/**
 * Creates UPDATE query and applies given update values.
 */
update(updateSet: QueryDeepPartialEntity<Entity>): UpdateQueryBuilder<Entity>;
/**
 * Creates UPDATE query for the given entity and applies given update values.
 */
update<Entity extends ObjectLiteral>(entity: EntityTarget<Entity>, updateSet?: QueryDeepPartialEntity<Entity>): UpdateQueryBuilder<Entity>;
```
The latter definition seems to work fine, however the first definition seems to be faulty. I think this is because an `Entity` is assingable to `QueryDeepPartialEntity<Entity>`, so using `.update(Person)` chooses the first definition. By using `.update(Person, {})` we explicitly use the second definition.

### Steps to reproduce

```ts
import { EntityManager } from 'typeorm';

class Person {}

const manager: EntityManager = 0 as any;
const builder = entityManager.createQueryBuilder().update(Person); // => UpdateQueryBuilder<any>
```

### My Environment

| Dependency          | Version  |
| ---                 | ---      |
| Operating System    |      Windows 11    |
| Node.js version     | 20.5.1 |
| Typescript version  | 5.1.3 |
| TypeORM version     | 0.3.19 |
